claims.text: The record contains conflicting allergy facts for codeine: a staff note states the patient is allergic to codeine per the pharmacy record, while a patient note denies allergy, describing only feeling sick once.

citations.quote: Allergic to codeine per the pharmacy record.
I am not allergic to codeine, I just felt sick once.

open_questions: Which medications were started, stopped, held or changed? The record provided contains no medication change entries.
Which follow-ups, referrals or tests are planned or outstanding? The record contains no follow-up, referral or test entries.
When was the codeine allergy or intolerance first recorded, and what reaction was documented at that time? The record does not give a date or prior reaction details.
Who documented the codeine allergy and on what basis? The staff note attributes it to the pharmacy record; the original documenting clinician is not identified.
What was the nature and timing of the sickness after codeine, and was it ever assessed as a true allergic reaction? The patient notes only 'felt sick once' with no timing or assessment documented.
Has codeine been prescribed or administered since the allergy was recorded, and was it tolerated? No such entries appear in the record.
Was any allergy clarification or allergy testing for codeine ever planned or carried out? No such plan or testing is documented.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Conflicting codeine allergy information exists: staff note records allergy per pharmacy record while patient note denies allergy. This affects safe prescribing decisions.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Clinician to reconcile the codeine allergy discrepancy with the patient and confirm the allergy status in the record.
